title: Thomas More (1478–1535)
hookLine: Henry VIII's chancellor, beheaded for conscience, joking on the scaffold
carry: the king's good servant, god's first

lines: ONE THING HE WOULD NOT SAY.
cards: London, July 1535. A man climbs a scaffold on Tower Hill. He's been in the Tower for over a year, and he's thin and gray.
The steps are shaky, so he turns to the officer beside him and says, more or less: help me up, and as for coming down, I'll manage that myself. He was well-known for jokes like that.
Not long ago he was Lord Chancellor to King Henry the Eighth, the king's friend, the man who wrote Utopia. And he's about to die because of one thing he would not say.

teach.h: A LAWYER, A FATHER, THE KING'S FRIEND.
teach.b: Thomas More was a London lawyer, a father of four, with a house full of books, children, animals and arguments. He gave his daughters the same serious education as a son, which was rare then.

He loved the law, and he loved his king. Then Henry wanted his marriage to Catherine of Aragon ended, and the Pope wouldn't do it. So Henry broke with Rome and had himself declared head of the Church in England.
More resigned as chancellor and went quiet.
In 1534 every leading subject was told to swear an oath that went with the king's new marriage and against the Pope's authority.
More refused, and here's the careful part: he refused silently. He never said why.
He believed that under English law, silence could not be treated as treason, so he held his tongue and trusted the law he'd served all his life. It didn't save him.
At his trial, a witness named Richard Rich testified to words More swore he never said. Only then, condemned, did More speak his mind about the Church.
On the scaffold, the story goes, he said he died the king's good servant, but God's first. He didn't hate the king. He just knew the order.
It's honest to add: as chancellor, More pursued Protestants hard, and some were burned in those years.

teach.h: A MARTYR, AND A HARD RECORD.
teach.b: Catholics honor him as a martyr of conscience, and historians still argue over that record.

teach.h: THE KING'S GOOD SERVANT, BUT GOD'S FIRST.
teach.b: The Church canonized him in 1935, and Pope John Paul the Second named him patron of politicians.

how: Catholics keep the feast of Saints Thomas More and John Fisher on June 22; many lawyers attend a yearly 'Red Mass', and More is invoked as patron of statesmen and politicians.

o: the lawyer-saint who died for an oath he wouldn't swear
a Protestant reformer burned during Henry's reign
the English king who broke with Rome to remarry

games.q: what's inside the story — tap the pairs.

s: More loudly denounced the king when asked to swear
he refused in silence and never said why, trusting that silence could not be called treason.
he joked on the way up the scaffold
help me up, he said, and coming down I'll manage myself.
More's record as chancellor is free of controversy
he pursued Protestants hard, and historians still argue over it.

games.q: you're Thomas More. the king demands you swear an oath you can't swear. what do you do?
o: swear it and keep your doubts to yourself.
refuse, and publicly condemn the king.
refuse, and say nothing about why.
games.why: he refused and stayed silent, trusting the law that silence isn't treason. only a witness's testimony, which More said was false, condemned him.

practice: Think of a promise you've made that nobody is checking: to call someone, to stop saying a certain thing, to be honest about something small.
Hold it quietly and decide to keep it; you don't have to tell anyone, the way More never explained himself. If you pray, you can ask Thomas More to pray for you, the way Catholics ask the saints.

wordCard.voice: Thomas More. Lawyer, father, chancellor, and a saint who died for what he would not swear, with a joke on his lips.

orig.note: Greek: no place. More built the name of his book Utopia from these two words.

carryVoice: Your line: the king's good servant, God's first. That ends a week of saints: Augustine, Patrick, Benedict and Scholastica, and listen, Clare, Catherine, Joan, and More. Day ninety-one.
